Modern.brandNameRationale: Two words. Off Grid is the customer's stated goal: to be somewhere the phone signal is weak and the city is far. The brand sits on the destination, not the equipment.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern outdoor brands are competing with the legacy giants (Patagonia, REI) and the technical specialists (Arc'teryx). The customer is design-literate, weight-conscious, and willing to pay for materials science that survives a long trip.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Topo Designs (topodesigns.com) holds the modern outdoor-lifestyle peer. Cotopaxi (cotopaxi.com) sits in the design-led middle. REI Co-op (rei.com) is the institutional retailer. Arc'teryx (arcteryx.com) holds the technical-premium peer. We sit closest to Topo in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: Outdoor gear for the trip that's two days too long.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Goes outside on weekends and books a real trip once a year. Buys the gear that lasts five trips. Reads the spec sheet.

dos: Show the gear, the material, the weight
Photograph real trips with real customers

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. OFF GRID in a tight modern grotesk, all caps, two words on one line. A small geometric mark, two crossed thin lines suggesting a compass bearing, used as the favicon and on every gear tag.

colorPalette.name: Trail Black
colorPalette.meaning: Wet rock, the dark of the early morning trail.

colorPalette.name: Hi-Vis Orange
colorPalette.meaning: Safety accent. The marker on a trail.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for material specs and weight
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the gear data (weight, gauge, material). The regular carries the brand.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No 'find yourself' copy. No empty-mountain photography. No celebrity-explorer partnerships. No 'wilderness lifestyle' bundles.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: A site that shows the gear in real use first. Real customer photos from real trips. A printed gear-guide twice a year. A monthly newsletter with three pieces of gear and where they've been tested.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words. Hawksworth sounds like an English country surname or place name with quiet outdoor heritage. Outfitters is the older word for a shop that supplies expeditions. The whole name reads as a heritage outfitter that has been outfitting walking parties and shooting parties for almost a century.
Luxury.story: Hawksworth Outfitters began as a small shop above a country gun makers. The current generation has stayed at the same address. Each item is hand-finished. Each customer is recorded in the same ledger started in 1932.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end outdoor has been moving toward technical performance and bigger marketing. There's a parallel market for heritage outfitters in the older tradition. Hand-finished gear, lifetime guarantees, decades-long relationships with shooting parties, walking clubs, and country families.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Holland & Holland (hollandandholland.com) holds the institutional peer in shooting and outdoor luxury. Purdey (purdey.com) sits at the bespoke firearm-and-outdoor tier. Filson (filson.com) does the heritage American workwear-and-outdoor middle. We sit smaller and more discreet than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A heritage outfitter making hand-finished gear for country pursuits.

targetAudience.primary: Wealthy, often inherited. Owns a country house. Walks, fishes, shoots. Buys gear once and expects it to last decades. Values the relationship with the outfitter.

dos: Name the material, the maker, the leatherworker
Send paper measurement cards for fittings
donts: Photograph the shop for fashion press

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn hawk silhouette becomes the outfitter's hallmark, used on the leather hangtag of every piece, the printed catalog, and the brass plaque outside the shop.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure client portal
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the few digital surfaces.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No wholesale to outdoor chains. No technical-performance marketing. No celebrity ambassadors. No social media presence. No press.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Pack is the act and the object. What you carry and what you carry it in. The brand sits on the smallest decision of any trip: what to take. Plain, direct, immediately useful.
Minimal.industrySummary: Outdoor brands have elaborate names and longer stories. There's an opening for one that strips it back to the verb and the object at once.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most outdoor brands fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some Japanese hiking brands and certain ultralight-backpacking practitioners' kit lists.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Outdoor gear designed to be carried, not collected.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who already know what they want to take outside. They want the gear, the weight, the price. They will not read the founder's letter.

dos: Show the gear, the weight, the price
donts: Photograph the gear against mountain backdrops
Use the word ultralight as marketing

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. PACK in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps, four letters with generous space. No icon. The tag, the catalog, and the receipt all carry the wordmark and nothing else.

typography.rationale: One face. The tag, the spec sheet, and the receipt all carry the same wordmark.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No seasonal lookbooks. No collaborations with fashion houses. No 'lifestyle' branded apparel. No newsletter.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Three words. Foundry suggests heavy production, durable engineering, and serious manufacturing. Outdoor Group names the category. The whole name reads like a real, established outdoor manufacturer already on the procurement panel at major retailers.
Corporate.industrySummary: Outdoor gear manufacturing and licensing is a B2B category dominated by giants (VF Corporation, Columbia Sportswear) and a few specialist firms. The buyers are retailers, brand licensees, and outdoor specialty chains. Brand and operational discipline are the differentiators.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: VF Corporation (vfc.com) holds the outdoor-conglomerate peer position. Columbia Sportswear (columbia.com) sits at the institutional tier. Amer Sports (amersports.com) is the international peer. We sit smaller, focused on the contemporary outdoor brand operator side.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Outdoor gear manufacturing and licensing for contemporary outdoor brands at scale.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Contemporary outdoor brands want operating partners with manufacturing depth and category understanding. The conglomerate giants are slow. We sit in the middle.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of Sourcing, VPs of Manufacturing, and Licensing Directors at outdoor brands, retail chains, and specialty outdoor chains. They sign multi-season production contracts.
motivations: Materials science and technical fabric expertise
One partner across apparel, packs, and hardware

dos: Show case studies with retail-partner performance
Speak to the buyer, not the end consumer

messagingPillars.name: Technical fabric expertise

messagingPillars.name: One partner across categories
messagingPillars.description: Apparel, packs, footwear, and accessories under one contract.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single mountain silhouette reduced to two intersecting strokes. Reads cleanly on a sourcing deck, name badge, and B2B trade show booth.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed catalogs and contracts
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed wholesale catalogs and licensing contracts.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No D2C consumer brand. No retail stores. No outdoor celebrity partnerships. The firm sells through B2B sourcing, not consumer outdoor social.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words, imperative. Get Lost is the customer's actual goal: to be somewhere they don't fully know. The brand puts the wandering in the brand position. Loud, slightly cheeky, and immediately legible.
Creative.manifesto: Most outdoor brands sell the photogenic mountain peak. The summit. The arrival. We made Get Lost because the actual experience of being outside is the wander before the destination. The wrong turn. The unmarked trail. The hour you sat by the river because you didn't know which way was the car. The brand is for the time spent not arriving.
Creative.industrySummary: Outdoor branding has been polished, summit-focused, and slightly aspirational. There's room for a brand that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the long, slow, slightly aimless time outside that nobody photographs.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Yeti (yeti.com) does the irreverent rugged middle. Topo Designs (topodesigns.com) holds the design-led modern. Howler Brothers (howlerbros.com) sits in the playful-outdoor peer position. We sit warmer and more honest than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: An outdoor brand for the hour you didn't plan.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Goes outside often. Doesn't summit. Sits by rivers. Pulls over for the view. Buys the gear because the brand made them laugh.

dos: Talk like the friend who's already in the parking lot

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the L of LOST stylized as a small turned arrow, suggesting a path that turns. Standalone turned-arrow icon for stickers, social profiles, and gear tags.

colorPalette.name: Trail Red
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, stickers

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and gear tags
typography.rationale: Migra has warmth and character. Neue Montreal handles the practical bits. The pair feels designed and a little weird.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a summit brand. Not a technical-spec brand. Not afraid of red. Not too cool to pull over for snacks.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Real customer photos from the parking lot, not the summit. Stickers in every order. A weekly newsletter with one good slow walk a week. A merch line of two shirts that say GET LOST across the back.
